newsitem.title: USA: Global debt issues driven by European/Asian demand.
newsitem.headline: Global debt issues driven by European/Asian demand.

text.p: Large corporations have been launching global offerings of U.S. dollar denominated debt in order to tap strong investor demand for such investments by European and Asian investors, syndicate officials said.
"This is a bet on the dollar triggered by the French elections," said one syndicate source. "Who wants to own francs and the euro when it looks like the European (Monetary) Union will fall apart?"
On Wednesday morning, Ford Motor Credit Corp, a unit of Ford Motor Co, sold $1 billion in 10-year bonds in a global offering via Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley.
The deal was marketed with price talk of around 60 basis points, but priced at 59 basis points over Treasuries, due to strong demand from global investors, a Merrill official said.
Market sources noted international investors have shown a strong appetite for 10-year paper, the longest maturity in which they typically invest.
"If you want to go long on dollars, you're not going to buy two-years. You make a long-duration bet," said one source.
